title: Sections of unramified and separated morphisms are open respectively closed immersions, and both for unramified separated morphisms

core_obligations: Part (1): a section of an unramified morphism is an open immersion, obtained because the graph of any S-morphism is the base change of the diagonal Delta_{X/S} and the diagonal of an unramified morphism is an open immersion (Morphisms, Lemma diagonal-unramified-morphism), immersions being stable under base change (Schemes, Lemma base-change-immersion).
Part (2): the separated analogue with the diagonal a closed immersion (Schemes, Definition separated).
Part (3): a section of an unramified separated morphism is both open and closed immersion, combining (1) and (2).
proof_roadmap: Fix base S; graph Gamma_f : X' -> X' x_S X equals the base change of Delta_{X/S} via the projection; separated resp. unramified makes the diagonal a closed resp. open immersion; base change preserves immersions; specialize X' = S for (1) and (2); (3) follows by combining.
difficulty_reason: Single graph-of-section = base change of diagonal argument; three parts combine one diagonal fact with base-change stability of immersions.
